The buffer flickered, unstable and already partly overwritten. Most of the lines were unreadable. But three remained long enough for him to copy them into his head.

RANCH DISCHARGE REDUCED

MESA RESPONSE DETECTED

ANCHOR SEARCH INITIATED

Then the buffer erased itself.

The central monitor returned to normal.

Birds crossed the eastern camera view, small and black against the brightening sky. They flew over the fence without hesitation. Nothing followed them. Nothing stopped them. Nothing in the daylight suggested the boundary had ever mattered.

The ranch made a faint effort at wrongness.

Camera Four blurred.

A livestock tag flickered.

The radiation monitor gave a weak pulse.

The system logged each event with calm approval.

Visual anomaly.

Telemetry interruption.

Localized discharge.

Routine.

Stable.

Contained.

Elias closed the official report without saving the visible screen. It did not matter. The system had already saved the lie.

Then he took the paper logbook, opened the back cover, and removed the folded copy.

At the top of the page, above the copied KYMO lines, he wrote a title.

THE 03:46 FILE

Beneath it, after a moment, he added:

Passive Watch Seven — Cedar Mesa Event

Mara watched him.

“This is a mistake,” she said.

“Probably.”

“That is not reassuring.”

“It wasn’t meant to be.”

For the first time all night, Mara almost smiled.

Almost.

Then it was gone.

“Hide it better than that,” she said.

Elias looked at her.

She looked back at him, expression steady, voice unreadable.

“I never said that.”

“No,” he said. “You didn’t.”

He folded the page again, smaller this time, and slipped it into the inner lining of the old analog binder labeled PV-7 ANALOG SUMMARY — YEAR ONE. Not perfect. Not permanent. But not digital. Not indexed. Not easily found by a system that trusted clean storage and official channels.

Outside, morning settled fully over Cedar Mesa Ranch.

The place looked ordinary now.

A restricted ranch. A quiet fence. A service road. A mesa line on the horizon that had not changed shape, had not moved closer, had not given any person driving past a reason to slow down and stare.

The danger had not ended.

It had become harder to see.

Elias sat back at the console and watched the feeds resume their familiar low-level wrongness. A little static. A little drift. A faint light that appeared once above the pasture and vanished before the camera could focus.

The system accepted it.

The log accepted it.

The station hummed around him as if the night had resolved.

The ranch had started making noise again.

This time, Elias knew better than to feel relieved.

chapters.title: Author’s Note
chapters.content:
Author’s Note

The Uintah Rift series began with a simple question: what if the strange stories surrounding a place were not the explanation, but only the surface of something much larger?

I have always been drawn to mysteries that sit at the edge of science, folklore, and the unknown. In this series, Utah is more than a setting. It is a threshold, a place where old stories, unexplained events, hidden systems, and human choices begin to collide.

At its heart, this series is not only about signals, anomalies, or what might exist beyond ordinary understanding. It is about the people asked to face the impossible and still make human decisions inside it. Slate and the team do not always have clear answers. Often, they have only evidence, instinct, fear, and the courage to keep asking better questions.

Thank you for entering the rift with me. I hope this story leaves you wondering what is beneath the surface, what we still do not understand, and what might happen when the world answers back.

chapters.title: The Story Continues
chapters.content:
The Story Continues

The events in Utah were only the beginning.

As the signals spread, the team begins to understand that the anomaly is not isolated beneath the mesa. It is part of something larger, older, stranger, and far more connected than anyone imagined. Each discovery raises a more dangerous question: is the system breaking apart, or has it been holding the world together all along?

Continue the Uintah Rift series as the mystery expands beyond Utah, beyond science, and beyond anything Slate and his team thought they were prepared to face.

Uintah Rift Series

Book 1: The Distortion Below When unexplained distortions begin beneath the Utah desert, Slate and his team discover that something ancient and unstable is operating below the surface—and it may be holding reality together in ways no one understands.

Book 2: The Fractured Signal As the anomaly spreads and signals begin to break, the team realizes Utah is not an isolated event but part of a larger pattern connecting sites across the world.

Book 3: The Hidden Lattice The team discovers that Utah is not the source of the anomaly, but a counterweight in a hidden lattice that is struggling to keep reality stable.

Book 4: The Shattered Node When one of the global nodes begins to fracture, governments and factions move toward control, while Slate’s team learns that interference may be the very thing making the system fail.

Book 5: The Final Resonance  As the network reaches its breaking point, Slate becomes the one presence the system responds to—not as a solution, but as a limit the world can no longer ignore.

Book 6: Terms of Crossing  With the world divided over containment, expansion, and control, humanity must face the truth that stability cannot be forced—and crossing into what comes next will require restraint.
